name: freeze-v1
status: candidate for review; tagged freeze-v1 only after a review PASS and the student's go-ahead, never edited afterwards
purpose: Everything that is fixed before any fraud-data (ULB, IEEE-CIS) result exists. Choices made with labels use ADBench only.

detectors.params_note: PyOD defaults, except PCA min_variance_ratio (components with explained-variance ratio <= 1e-10 are dropped; a documented modification of PyOD's PCA). contamination is unused: no detector threshold is used.
detectors.ecod: train-only re-implementation: ECDFs and skewness signs fixed at fit time (PyOD 3.6.7 ECOD is batch-dependent)
detectors.knn_lof_training_scores: leave-one-out (a row is not its own neighbour)

knn_lof_fit_sample.seed: split seed; 0 when the split has none (ULB, IEEE-CIS)

detectors.score_direction: higher = more anomalous for every detector

E-bench.source: lowest average FP@K rank among the 20 triples, min-max + mean, 15 ADBench sets, 2% budget (supervisor, 2026-10-29)
E-bench.note: identical to E-lit; the paper states this coincidence. Friedman over the 20 triples: p 0.976 (2%), 0.419 (5%), all within the Nemenyi CD, so the triples cannot be told apart

E-bench-5%.source: the E-bench rule at the 5% ADBench budget

E-all.source: all six detectors: the 'bigger is better?' control

fusion.calibrators: fitted per member on that member's training scores only; min-max not clipped; percentile = share of training scores <= s

ulb.fitted_on: day-1 training scores of each method (fused training scores for ensembles)
ulb.check: alert count and FPR on day 2 vs the budget implied by the quantile

rules.k_definition: K = max(1, ceil(budget * n_test)), with budget * n_test rounded to 9 decimals first
rules.ties: expected value: rows tied with the K-th score share the remaining alert slots in proportion, so row order never decides an alert
rules.zero_variance_member: under z-score calibration a member with constant training scores (range exactly 0) maps to 0
rules.zero_variance_member_status: supervisor confirmation pending; 0 cases on ADBench and ULB training data (results/tables/setup/zero_variance.csv)

adbench.source: Minqi824/ADBench classical .npz files at the commit pinned in src/thesis/download.py
adbench.selection_rule: 1,000-50,000 rows, at most 100 features, anomaly rate at most 10%, 13_fraud excluded (it is ULB)
adbench.duplicates: kept (files as distributed); duplicate-aware robustness check with --dedup; not a full reproduction of the ADBench protocol

ulb.features: V1-V28 and log1p(Amount); Time is the split variable only
ulb.split: day 1 (Time < 86400 s) fit, day 2 test; every training row strictly earlier than every test row

data.preprocessing: z-score of every detector input with training-split statistics (constant columns get scale 1)
data.labels: never passed to fit(), scalers, calibrators or thresholds

score_cache.note: key = hash of detector params, KNN/LOF fit sample size, preprocessing, PyOD version and the ECOD variant

baselines.default_iforest: IForest with the PyOD defaults above: the realistic practitioner pick
baselines.oracle_best_single: the single detector with the lowest FP@K on the test window, chosen with test labels: an upper bound, not a deployable method
